hypotheses.justification: Every ring already carries the canonical instance `algebraInt A : Algebra ℤ A`, built from `[CommRing A]`. So if this binder is deleted, `aeval (R := ℤ) a` still elaborates, using `algebraInt A`, and the statement is otherwise unchanged. Any two `Algebra ℤ A` instances are equal (there is only one ring hom ℤ →+* A), so the theorem stays true. The same proof goes through unchanged. `rw [hom_eval₂]` turns the left side into `Φ.eval₂ (g.comp (aeval a).toRingHom) (g b)`. After `congr 1`, the goal is equality of two ring homs `ℤ[X] →+* B`. `Polynomial.ringHom_ext'` reduces this to two goals. The ℤ part is closed by `RingHom.ext_int`, which holds for any ring homs out of ℤ. The `X` part, `g (aeval a X) = aeval (g a) X`, is closed by `simp` via `aeval_X`. None of these steps depends on which `Algebra ℤ` instance is used. There are no degenerate cases to worry about: the zero ring also has the canonical instance. This binder can be deleted together with `[Algebra ℤ B]`, or on its own.

The argument is the same as for `[Algebra ℤ A]`. `[CommRing B]` already gives the canonical `algebraInt B`, so `aeval (R := ℤ) (g a)` still elaborates. All `Algebra ℤ B` instances agree, so the statement stays true. The proof `rw [hom_eval₂]; congr 1; refine Polynomial.ringHom_ext' (RingHom.ext_int _ _) ?_; simp` does not depend on the choice of instance: `RingHom.ext_int` handles the ℤ part, and `aeval_X` handles `X`. This binder can be deleted on its own, or together with `[Algebra ℤ A]`.
